## What

The headline benefit of blueprint-izing a learning loop
(`deterministic-blueprints-migration-2026-06-13` D-001): a blueprint is a
**distributable artifact** — export it, install it on another pot, run it there
— which a baked-in lib+routine can never be. P-112 proves that round-trip for the
`negative-space` pilot (P-110). This page is the reusable recipe + the two
gotchas that will otherwise burn an hour.

## The round-trip has four legs — prove them with the REAL machinery

The proof lives in
`packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint-steps/negative-space-marketplace-roundtrip.test.ts`:

1. **export** — package the bundled blueprint dir
   (`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/<id>/`) into the official
   multi-blueprint repo layout `<repo>/<id>/blueprint.yaml`. This is exactly the
   shape `scripts/publish-official-blueprints.mts sync` regenerates the public
   mirror (`github.com/Papercusp/blueprints`) from — so copying the bundle dir is
   a faithful export.
2. **install** — `installBlueprintFromCupboardCore` (the core the
   `POST /api/cupboard/install-blueprint` route wraps) into a **fresh**
   installed-blueprints dir = a second pot's installed tier. Stub only the
   git-clone binary (copy the packaged repo) — the same DI seam
   `install-blueprint-core.test.ts` / `resolve-and-install.e2e.test.ts` use.
   Note: the install core now calls `registerHarnessOpProxies` on any `ops:`
   manifest entries BEFORE the resolve+validate step (P-002) — so a blueprint
   that ships its own harness ops validates clean rather than failing
   `unknown-op`. The test stubs don't need to wire this; it fires automatically.
3. **resolve** — `makeComposedResolveExtends({ installedDir, builtin })` now
   returns the **installed** path for the id, not the built-in: the marketplace
   copy *shadows* the bundled built-in (assert the resolver flips pre→post
   install — that is the distribution win in one line).
4. **run** — load the installed copy with `resolveAndValidateBlueprint(raw,
   resolver)` and run it through `runProgramCore` + `inlineRunOp`. Inject the
   op's test deps (`setNegativeSpaceScanDeps`) so the tick never touches PG.
   Assert it reaches a clean `done` AND stays dark (no-op, `skipReason:flag-off`)
   when its flag is off — behavior-neutral in the new pot too (D-004).
5. **fire (production path)** — drive the *real* `handleBlueprintRun`
   (`system:blueprint-run`) with `{ blueprintId: '<id>' }` and point its launch
   resolver at the installed copy via `setLaunchBlueprintResolver` (the same seam
   the operator overrides for installed/Cupboard launch blueprints). It detects
   program-mode and runs the program inline — proving the installed blueprint
   fires through the production trigger, not just a direct `runProgramCore` call.

Net: a host that has **never** seen the blueprint in its installed tier acquires
it via the Cupboard path and runs it — the thing a lib+routine cannot do.

## The two gotchas

- **The live `:3070` operator is GREEN (`main`); a freshly-migrated blueprint is
  on `staging`.** So `blueprint:catalog` / the live Cupboard surfaces will NOT
  show a just-migrated blueprint (e.g. `negative-space`) until the staging→green
  deploy carries it. Don't conclude the migration is broken — check the tier you
  are hitting. The staging operator (`:3170`) has it.
- **The live install route hard-requires a public `https://github.com/...` URL**
  (`GITHUB_URL_RE` in `install-blueprint-core.ts`), and the install writes to the
  shared `~/.papercusp/blueprints/<id>/` (shadowing the built-in for **every**
  peer on the box, per the `papercusp-root` / `PAPERCUSP_HOME` pin caveat). So a
  *live* local round-trip is not the move on the shared dev box — prove the
  mechanism via the install **core** (dependency-injected) in a test, and treat
  the live public-Comb publish/install as owner-gated.

## Completing the live leg (owner-gated)

> Done once, live, 2026-06-13 (owner-authorized, **private** repos): a private
> `papercupai/*` repo + the real `POST /api/cupboard/install-blueprint` route
> (gh-https-authed private clone) + a staging-runner run of the installed copy
> — dark (flag off → zero mining), distinct id (no built-in shadow), no
> `harness:create` (no cadence routine materialized). See
> `deterministic-blueprints-migration-2026-06-13` D-016. Key gotcha: a live
> install requires the **distinct-id** guard or it shadows the shared built-in
> for every peer on the box.

Outward-facing + credential-gated; do not run autonomously without an owner OK:

1. Deploy P-010/P-110 to green (green-checkpoint FF, or
   `npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts --execute`).
2. `node scripts/publish-official-blueprints.mts sync` — regenerate + push the
   public mirror (papercupai creds) so it includes the blueprint.
3. Publish the listing: `scripts/publish-official-blueprints.mts publish --ids
   <id>` (or `POST /api/cupboard/publish-blueprint { id, github_url, listing_ref }`).
4. On a second pot: `POST /api/cupboard/install-blueprint { listingId }` (or
   `{ githubUrl, listingRef }`), then `harness:create { blueprintId: <id> }` in
   the pot — its `triggers.schedule` cadence fires `system:blueprint-run`.
